candidate.statement: Addition of bevacizumab to chemotherapy regimens significantly prolongs progression-free survival in metastatic colorectal cancer patients.
queries: bevacizumab colorectal cancer progression-free survival randomized trial
bevacizumab chemotherapy colorectal cancer PFS benefit
bevacizumab metastatic colorectal cancer PFS hazard ratio

review.rationale: MED:42583256 reports the final results of a randomized clinical trial in chemorefractory metastatic colorectal cancer comparing trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) chemotherapy plus bevacizumab versus FTD-TPI monotherapy alone. Progression-free survival was significantly prolonged with the addition of bevacizumab (4.6 months vs 2.4 months; HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.31-0.73), directly supporting the hypothesis that adding bevacizumab to chemotherapy improves PFS in metastatic colorectal cancer.

candidate.statement: Among patients with BRAF V600E-mutant colorectal cancer, encorafenib-based therapy confers significantly improved progression-free survival compared to non-encorafenib standard regimens.
queries: encorafenib BRAF V600E metastatic colorectal cancer progression-free survival

review.rationale: Multiple randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses directly evaluate encorafenib-based therapy versus standard non-encorafenib regimens in patients with BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer. For instance, the BREAKWATER Cohort 3 randomized trial (MED:42219860) demonstrated statistically significant improvement in PFS with encorafenib plus cetuximab and FOLFIRI compared to control FOLFIRI +/- bevacizumab (HR 0.44, 15.2 vs 8.3 months, p = 0.0002). The NAUTICAL randomized phase II trial (MED:41852303) also confirmed superior PFS for encorafenib plus cetuximab versus irinotecan-based control regimens (HR 0.37, 4.2 vs 2.5 months, p = 0.0004). Systematic reviews and health agency evaluations (MED:42358834, MED:42154933) further confirm that encorafenib-based therapy significantly improves PFS over non-encorafenib standard regimens in this specific population.

review.rationale: The candidate hypothesis examines the association between female sex and progression-free survival in colorectal cancer within a subgroup defined by research signatures A and B.
